arch_zon_EdmZones: RULE: City of Edmonton, Charter Bylaw 20001 Zoning Bylaw, as adopted (effective 1 Jan 2024; City PDF, local text data/raw/edm/bylaw/b.txt; amendments since not checked ?), s. 2.120 BE, s. 2.130 IM, s. 2.140 IH: BE permitted uses incl. Minor Industrial (2.3), Food and Drink Service (2.8), Indoor Sales and Service (2.10), Major and Minor Indoor Entertainment (2.11, 2.12), Outdoor Sales and Service (2.16), Child Care Service (2.18), Community Service (2.19), Minor Utility (2.22), Urban Agriculture (2.25); 3.2.1 Minor Industrial 'must be located within an enclosed building'; 3.3.1 Bars, Food and Drink, Health Services, Major Indoor Entertainment 'maximum Floor Area is 500 m2 per individual establishment'; 3.7.1 Indoor Sales and Service 500 m2; 3.12.1 Community Services 'The maximum Floor Area is 500 m2 per individual establishment' (no shelter exception in adopted text); 3.16.1 Urban Agriculture 'within or on a building'; 3.18 variance to floor-area caps with mitigation for 'on-Site or Abutting non-Industrial Uses'; Table 4.1 height 16.0 m, FAR 1.6; 5.3.2 'A maximum of 10% of Ground Floor windows facing a Street ... may be covered by non-transparent material'; 5.8 loading not between building and Street. IM: Major Industrial 'limited to those existing as of January 1, 2024' (2.3), Minor Industrial (2.4), Indoor Sales and Service limited to existing or animal hospitals (2.7), Office (2.8, 300 m2 per establishment 3.5.1), Outdoor Sales and Service (2.9), Special Event (2.11), Minor Utility (2.13), Urban Agriculture (2.16); 3.2.2 accessory temporary employee sleeping not 'suitable for use as permanent residence'; Table 4.1 height 18.0 m, FAR 2.0. IH: Major Industrial (2.1), Minor Industrial 'limited to those existing as of January 1, 2024' (2.2), Major and Minor Utility (2.4, 2.5); 3.1.1 office/display <=33%; Table 4.1 minimum Site 1.0 ha, height 30.0 m, FAR 2.0 — https://www.edmonton.ca/sites/default/files/public-files/assets/Bylaws/Bylaw20001.pdf
arch_zon_Edm720: RULE: City of Edmonton, Zoning Bylaw 20001 (as adopted, eff. 1 Jan 2024), s. 7.20 General Rules of Interpretation: subs. 3.3.2 'where specific purposes or activities do not conform to any Use definition or generally conform to the wording of 2 or more Use definitions, the Development Planner may deem the purposes or activities to conform to a Use they consider to be the most appropriate. In this situation, despite any other Section of this Bylaw, the Use is always considered a Discretionary Use'; 3.3.3 'The list of Uses within each Zone determines the types of activities allowed within each Zone'; 1.8.3 'industrial building' means 'a building containing 1 or more Industrial Uses'; 1.8.7 'non-residential building' contains '1 or more non-Residential Uses' — https://www.edmonton.ca/sites/default/files/public-files/assets/Bylaws/Bylaw20001.pdf
arch_zon_EdmDefs: RULE: City of Edmonton, Zoning Bylaw 20001 (as adopted), s. 8.10 Use Definitions and s. 8.20 General Definitions: Minor Industrial = processing, 'manufacturing, cleaning, servicing, repairing or testing materials, goods and equipment', storing, etc., nuisance 'less impactful than ... Major Industrial'; Minor Indoor Entertainment examples 'fitness facilities, gyms'; Major Indoor Entertainment examples 'aquariums, arenas ... museums ... sports or entertainment complexes'; Outdoor Sales and Service examples incl. 'plant nurseries'; Urban Agriculture examples 'hydroponic or aquaponic systems, and vertical farms'; Food and Drink Service 'cafes, juice bars, and restaurants'; Indoor Sales and Service 'retail, personal service'; Residential 'designed for people to live in'; Minor Utility examples incl. 'switching centres, telecommunications centres'; 8.20 'Accessory means a Use, building or structure that is naturally or normally incidental, subordinate, and devoted to the principal Use or building, and located on the same Lot or Site'; 'Site means an area of land consisting of 1 or more Abutting Lots'; 'Use means the purposes or activities for which a piece of land or its buildings are designed, arranged, developed or intended' — https://www.edmonton.ca/sites/default/files/public-files/assets/Bylaws/Bylaw20001.pdf
